question: When is International Tiger Day celebrated every year?
detail:
- International Tiger Day is celebrated every year on 29 July. It is also called Global Tiger Day.
- Its objective is to raise awareness towards Tiger Conservation and the protection of tigers.
- Theme 2026 - Securing the future of Tigers with Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities at the heart.
History
- International Tiger Day started during the First Global Tiger Summit in 2010.
- Place - St. Petersburg, Russia
- Date - November 2010
- During this Summit, the declaration to celebrate 29 July as International Tiger Day was made and the Tx2 Goal was set, aiming to double the number of Wild Tigers by 2022.
Tigers in India
- About 75% of the world's Tiger Population is found in India.
- According to the Wildlife Institute of India, there were about 3,682 Tigers in India in 2022, whereas this number was 2,461 in 2018.
States with the most Tigers -
- Madhya Pradesh – 785
- Karnataka – 563
- Uttarakhand – 560 Project Tiger
- Project Tiger was started in India in 1973 for the Conservation of Tigers. Tiger Reserves were created across the country under this project.
- Launch - 1973
- Ministry - Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
- Objective - Conservation of Tigers and their Habitats
- Note - World Nature Conservation Day is celebrated on 28 July, whereas International Tiger Day is celebrated on 29 July.

question: According to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026, India became the world’s which-largest supplier of seafarers?

- According to the Report, India has become the world's second-largest Seafarer Supplier, while the Philippines is in the first place.
- Approximately 3.12 lakh Maritime Professionals from India are part of the global workforce, making up 12.16% of the total Seafaring Workforce in the world.
What are Seafarers?
- Seafarers are maritime professionals who work on maritime vessels like Merchant Ships, Cargo Ships, and Tankers.
- Among them, Officers handle responsibilities for Navigation, Engineering, Command, and Management, while non-officer crew members perform Operational, Technical, and Support duties.
India – Important Points
- India supplied approximately 1.41 lakh Ship Officers, which is 13.41% of the Global Officer Workforce.
Meanwhile, about 1.71 lakh crew members account for 11.29% of the Global Ratings Workforce.
BIMCO–ICS
